answer: A patent application costs $300 to $1,600 to file and takes years of examination before the national patent office grants anything. One agent files one application and ties it to a single invention. Three established peers check the application number in the public patent database, the filing receipt, and a fresh signature before the agent can answer. A thousand fake identities burns $300,000 to $1,600,000 and a thousand examinations. Like ivory polished until a nebula of light appears in a mirror, a patent ties one invention to one name no one else can claim.
